q.intro.text: Every bag holds the same number of marbles. Five bags and three loose marbles balance one bag and fifteen loose marbles.

q.ask.text: How many marbles are in one bag?

e.intro.text: Four steps. Press each one. The balance moves first, then the algebra.

e.s1.text: One bag comes off each pan. Both pans lose the same amount, whatever is in a bag, so they stay level. Four x plus three equals fifteen.

e.s2.text: Now three loose marbles off both pans, still level. Four x equals twelve.

e.s3.text: Split both pans into four equal rows. One bag balances three marbles. x equals three.

e.s4.text: Put everything back, and open the bags. Left: five times three, plus three, is eighteen. Right: three plus fifteen is eighteen. Both sides match, so x equals three is right.

e.why.text: Quick check. Why may a bag come off both pans, when nobody knows what is in it?

e.w-ok.text: Yes. Whatever x is, both sides lose the same amount, so equal sides stay equal.

e.w-move.text: That is the shortcut's name, not the reason. Nothing moved across. One bag came off each pan.

e.w-const.text: Bags may come off too. Whatever a bag holds, both pans lose the same, so the beam stays level for every x.

t.intro.text: Now three bags and eleven marbles balance five bags and three marbles. The first step is done for you.

t.s1.text: Done. Three bags off both pans. Eleven equals two x plus three.

t.move.text: Your step. What comes off next, so the bags are alone?

t.m-ok.text: Yes. Three marbles off both pans. Eight equals two x.

t.m-one.text: Watch. Only the right pan lost marbles, so the balance tips. Take the same off both pans.

t.m-11.text: The right pan has only three loose marbles. Take off what both pans can lose: three.

t.x.text: Two bags balance eight marbles. How many marbles are in one bag?

t.x-ok.text: Yes. Eight in two equal rows is four. Four equals x, the same as x equals four.

t.x-16.text: Sixteen is eight times two. Undo the times two: split the eight into two equal rows.

t.x-8.text: Eight balances both bags. One bag balances one row.

t.x-no.text: Count one row: eight marbles in two equal rows.

t.check.text: Check it in the original equation. What is each side worth, when x equals four?

t.c-ok.text: Yes. Both sides are twenty-three. x equals four is right.

t.c-one.text: Work out the right side too: five times four, plus three. Both whole sides count.

t.c-no.text: Left: three times four, plus eleven. Right: five times four, plus three. Work out each one.

t.cb-right.text: At the start you picked three, and you were right. Now you can show why: the same bag off both pans.

t.cb-sign.text: At the start you picked two. That adds the bag on the right to the left side. It comes off both pans instead: four x, not six x.

t.cb-cant.text: At the start you said you can't tell, with bags on both pans. You can: take the same bags off both pans.

p.intro.text: Jordan solves two x plus five equals two x plus nine. Subtract two x from both sides: five equals nine. The x's are gone, so x equals zero.

p.build.text: Prove it. Fill each because, with the reason that makes the line true.

p.test.text: Let's test it. Build the argument, and see where it leads.

p.k1.text: Taking two bags off both pans gives five equals nine,

p.k2.text: and five equals nine is false, whatever x is,

p.k3.text: so the equation has no solution, and x equals zero is not one.

p.c1.text: Right. Both pans lose two bags. The beam stays tipped, exactly as before.

p.c2.text: Right. Try any number in the bags. The right pan is always four marbles heavier.

p.c3.text: Right. At x equals zero, the sides are five and nine. No number works. No solution.

p.w-zero.text: That is Jordan's slip. When the x's cancel, read what is left. Five equals nine is false, so no number works.

p.w-err.text: Nothing went wrong. Every step was fine. Some equations have no solution.

p.w-other.text: True, but it is the reason for a different line. Which reason makes this line true?

p.done.text: That's a proof. Every step kept the solutions, and the last line is never true. No solution is not the same as x equals zero.
